projects.title: Show HN: Minimal dbt-style SQL builds with DuckDB and Make
projects.author: ltrg
projects.summary: "DuckDB and Make are all you need!" I love the ergonomics of dbt for building reproducible data pipelines with DuckDB -- particularly the ability to define output tables as individual `SELECT` queries and have them refer to each other -- but have always found the configuration and boilerplate excessive for the projects I work on. With the recent Rust rewrite of dbt Core, now seemed like a good time to consider the bits I actually need/use. Recently, I realised that DuckDB itself can parse SQL queries into an AST representation using the `json_serialize_sql` function. duckdb.mk (~250 lines `include`d in your Makefile) takes advantage of this to generate Make rules for your models automatically, and works with both DuckDB 1.4.1+ and 2.0 preview. Write a neat directory of SQL statements querying local and remote data, get a neat directory of Parquet files (plus a Mermaid diagram of the DAG) back. When you rebuild a table, duckdb.mk keeps track of dependencies (including remote resources queried over HTTP) and only rebuilds those that need it. This system is a distillation of various ad hoc solutions cooked up while working on data journalism and research projects over the past 5-10 years, most recently doing Observable-based research notebooks with Data Desk: https://research.datadesk.eco/ It's very much a starting point for further development, and contributions in line with the general minimalist philosophy are very welcome! Check out the `example/` directory for a simple test project that attributes satellite-observed methane plumes to oil and gas infrastructure using public data.

projects.title: Show HN: Obsidian Plugin for OpenModelica

projects.summary: I created an Obsidian plugin that serves as a front-end for OpenModelica that allows you to model and simulate cyber-physical systems (mechanical, fluid, magnetic, thermal, etc.) or a mix of all these systems all inside Obsidian. What is special about Modelica is that it is acausal: components do not have fixed input/output roles. You describe physical relationships with equations and connections, and the equations do not need to be written in a step-by-step order. Modelica (language) or OpenModelica (software) flattens the model into a simultaneous equation system (a system of differential algebraic equations (DAEs)) and then determines the computational causality and order needed to simulate it. As a disclaimer, I used AI to build it but not in a sloppy way. I have spent a lot of time testing it and making sure it's functional and accurate. And I hope it may help others to utilize such an underrated tool for learning/researching, as this is my main usage for it.

projects.title: Show HN: Digitron – a virtual analog synth and sequencer
projects.author: sillydevices
projects.summary: I’ve just released Digitron on iOS. It’s a virtual analog synthesizer with a sequencer. If I had to describe the rough idea, I’d say it’s something like a child of a Moog and a Pocket Operator. I started working on it about four years ago, mostly out of boredom. I was tired of building similar client-server apps that, in the end, were mostly different ways of displaying lists. I wanted to build something self-contained. The first version of Digitron was pretty simple: a 16-step sequencer and a monophonic synth with two oscillators and cross-modulation. I wrote the first audio engine in Kotlin. As long as it was rendering WAV files offline, everything sounded fine. But the first time I tried running it in real time on Android, the popcorn noises made it pretty obvious that this wasn’t going to work. So I rewrote the entire engine in C++, and along the way got much more familiar with real-time audio, DSP, optimization, and aliasing than I had originally planned. Over the next few years Digitron grew quite a bit: I added a patchbay, a more capable sequencer with patterns and parameter locks, 8 independent engines, a mixer, effects, polyphony, and a recorder, and I’ve surely forgotten something. The result is a fairly monstrous thing with a steep learning curve. But if you’re familiar with modular synths, it should be possible to find your way around it. The current Digitron stack is Kotlin Multiplatform for the application layer, backed by a cross-platform C++ audio engine. On Android it talks to the native layer through JNI, while on iOS I use Swift wrappers around the same C++ backend. The work on Digitron’s audio engine also eventually led to a new open-source project called PatchCore — a redesigned, more general-purpose modular audio engine: https://github.com/SillyDevices/PatchCore After about four years of working on it, it feels pretty strange to finally see Digitron in the App Store. I'd love to hear what you think about the synth.

projects.summary: 做了个小工具站，肽计算器： https://peptidecal.net 一句话说明：把瓶身上的数字（瓶重 + 加水量）换算成 U-100 针管的刻度。 为什么做？ 直说：这个需求已经有一堆工具了。我搜的时候翻了前几个，功能上确实都差不多——填瓶重、填加水量、填你自己要的剂量，出针管刻度。 但翻了一圈肽用户的真实反馈，很多人都还卡在“要加多少水来复溶“的这一步，所以首页的计算器做成了一个双模式的版本： - 还没有复溶的：适合还未复溶的用户。输入瓶内总量和想注射的量后，工具会给出一个建议加水量（以及对应浓度），并显示最终要抽取注射的毫升数以及 U-100 上的刻度。 - 已复溶的：适合已复溶，知道加水量（或已知浓度）的用户。输入想注射的量后，工具会直接换算出目标量对应的 抽取毫升数和 U-100 注射器刻度。 分成两条入口，默认用户还没有加水。而不是塞进一个表单让你自己判断该填哪个。 静态站，Cloudflare Workers 托管，纯 vanilla JS ，没有框架。计算链是固定的：mg （肽）→ mL （液体）→ units （针管刻度），改前面一个值后面顺着变。 站点刚上线，尤其想听听大家对下面几点的意见： 1. 两种模式是否容易理解？ 2. 换算逻辑上有没有我没想到的边界情况？ 3. 手机上的输入和阅读有没有不顺手的地方？ 欢迎拍砖。研究用途，不构成医疗建议。

projects.title: 做了一个面部评分站 face-rating.net：模型在浏览器本地跑，照片全程不出设备，求拍砖
projects.author: changhej
projects.summary: 做了一个面部评分站 face-rating.net：模型在浏览器本地跑，照片全程不出设备，求拍砖 链接： https://face-rating.net ## 这是什么 一个面部评分工具。一张正面照，浏览器里的图像模型给一个 10 分制的分。不用注册、不用邮箱，**照片不上传**。目前全站免费，没有付费墙，也没有订阅。 ## 分数是怎么来的 1. 浏览器里的关键点模型先测出 478 个面部关键点（ MediaPipe Face Mesh ，468 点 + 10 个虹膜点）。**这一步不出分数。** 2. 用眼睛的位置把照片摆正、裁到脸部，裁剪时不拉伸五官。 3. 一个**本地**图像模型读裁剪图，再读它的**镜像版**，两次预测取平均，换算成 10 分。 4. 这个模型是在**人类照片评分数据**上训练的——所以它输出的是学到的偏好，不是普世审美标准。这点我写在页面上了，不想含糊过去。 ## 几何读数是另一回事，不参与评分 同一批关键点还能算出对称性、纵向横向间距、脸型、眼角角度。很多人以为这些是分数的「成分」，**不是**。分数来自图像模型，几何来自关键点，两者不相乘也不相加。页面上和 FAQ 里我都逐个说明了。 ## 「本地」具体是什么意思 模型文件跟页面一起下载，照片和所有中间产物都在浏览器内存里——不上传、服务器没副本、刷新就没了。网站上没有任何一条上传照片的路径。隐私政策里写明：不用你的照片训练模型、不出售面部数据、不把照片或分数给广告方；站上第三方只有 Cloudflare （托管与安全）和邮件服务商。 ## 现在免费的都有什么 - 10 分制评分 - 六项单项工具：Golden Ratio Face Calculator 、Face Shape Detector 、Canthal Tilt Test 、Face Symmetry Test 、Jawline Rating 、Recessed Chin （最后一个用侧脸照） - 一篇 guide：Asymmetric Face （不对称脸的原因、哪些偏方没证据、怎么自己量） - 结果能存成一张本地生成的卡片，分享与否你自己定 ## 我刻意没做的几件事 - **不发布平均分、不发布百分位。** 免费分数我根本不收集，也没有有代表性的样本，说你比 X% 的人好看只能说明我测了谁。 - **不说这是医学、皮肤科或心理判断**，也不建议用它决定要不要面诊。 - **不鼓励跨工具比分数。** 不同工具测的可能不是一个量，你上传的多半也不是同一张照片——照片条件带来的差异往往比工具之间还大。 - 黄金比例那套「美不美」的说法在学术上争议很大，页面上引了四篇论文（含 2024 年那篇质疑它的），出处都放出来你自己判断。 ## 已知局限 - 正面照测不准下巴和鼻子的前后突出度，那两个需要侧脸照——2D 的硬限制。 - 同条件下可复现；**换了光线、表情、相机距离数字就会变。变的是照片，不是你。** - 首次打开要下模型，会等几秒，这也是我最想知道体验好不好的一点。 ## 想听什么 - 首次加载模型多久？手机上能忍吗？ - 分数出来后你会不会想知道「这数是怎么算的」——上面那段讲清楚了吗？ - 结果页是不是信息过载？ - 哪个几何读数对你真有用，哪个是废话？ 拍砖随意。要说「这玩意儿助长容貌焦虑」——这个批评我接，所以百分位、排名、平均分我都砍了，分数也不留在服务器上。有更好的做法欢迎提。

projects.title: 【开源自荐】Gear：根据任务测评自进化的 Agent 框架
projects.author: YehuiTang0316

github.name: rsi-gear/gear
github.description: Gear (General Evolution Architecture) is RSI infrastructure for AI agents. Use Gear to refine agent harnesses.

projects.summary: 大家好，自荐一个开源项目 Gear，希望帮助开发者提升 AI Agent 在具体任务中的表现。 开发 Agent 时，经常需要反复调整提示词、工具和执行流程，再跑一遍任务，检查改动是否有效。Gear 把这个过程组织成一个由评测反馈驱动的优化循环： 1. 准备一组有明确验收标准的任务，可以使用现有 benchmark，也可以定义自己的任务集。 2. 运行 Agent，收集执行轨迹和评测结果。 3. 由负责优化的 Agent 分析失败原因，修改授权范围内的组件。 4. 重新评测、比较候选版本，保留表现更好的方案，继续迭代。 可优化的组件包括提示词、工具实现、Skills、工作流和上下文管理。这些围绕模型的运行配置统称为 harness。Gear 会记录各版本的改动和评测结果，方便检查和复用；开发者也可以定制搜索算法，并根据通过率、费用或 token 消耗设置优化目标。 在项目公开的 AutomationBench Marketing 实验中，GPT 5.6 Luna + DSH 在 100 个公开任务上的任务通过率从 27% 提升到 53%，目标完成率从 75.37% 提升到 88.88%。这组结果包含 harness 优化和推理档位从 medium 到 max 的变化，且任务集参与过优化；实验配置与评分口径均已公开，便于读者判断结果的适用范围。 Gear 通过 Refine Skill 接入 Codex、Claude Code、DSH 等 Agent 环境。负责提出改进的 Agent 与执行任务的 Agent 可以使用不同模型。当前已支持 harness 优化，模型训练仍处于实验阶段。 项目采用 MIT 协议，提供中文文档和完整实验案例，欢迎试用、反馈和贡献。 GitHub 源码 中文文档与快速开始 实验过程与优化算法

projects.title: Show HN: Ox – A local agent that uses the internet for you
projects.author: ziyzhu
projects.summary: I’ve been building Ox, a local, open-source agent that uses the internet for you. Ox acts as an intelligent proxy between you and the internet. It uses websites and apps on your behalf, freeing you from attention-hungry interfaces and slow legacy services. As it works, it can turn what it learns into reusable actions (basically function calls), making future interactions deterministic and way faster. Most service integrations today are still built ahead of time: someone writes an API integration, connector, MCP server, or browser automation and then maintains it as the service changes. But the internet is becoming more dynamic so have our agents. With Ox, instead of waiting for a connector, you can say something like: “Connect to <service>.” Ox can study a website or workflow through capabilities it already has, turn what it learns into typed actions and reusable skills, validate them, and make them available immediately. That pushed me toward local agents. A local agent operates from your own device, network, and existing authenticated browser sessions instead of relying on shared datacenter infrastructure. This also makes it less likely to hit blocks aimed at datacenter IPs or centralized browser automation. The model doesn’t need your passwords, cookies, or session tokens. Authentication and browser state are owned by the Host, while the agent interacts through explicit actions that could be gated. Ox is completely free and open source. You can use any model provider, including local or self-hosted models, while keeping your agent’s data on device. As local models improve, I think this architecture becomes increasingly useful because the agent can become more capable without requiring more of your data to leave your device. The security model is also a big part of the design. Ox asks before taking sensitive actions, keeps credentials isolated from the model, limits what agent code can access, and lets you stop execution at any time. Underneath the app is OpenOx, an open protocol for self-evolving agents. It separates the interface, agent, model provider, persistent state, execution environment, and external capabilities. The agent can run JavaScript inside a capability-limited VM. The VM has no direct network access, Host filesystem access, shell, Node.js, or DOM. Anything outside the VM has to go through an explicit ox.* capability exposed by the Host. Services provide typed actions for websites, device capabilities, or MCP servers. Skills provide reusable instructions for combining those actions. New services and skills can be attached at runtime without waiting for a new version of the app. They can remain local or be recorded in Git and shared through repositories, so each Ox can evolve independently while benefiting from capabilities learned by others. The agent’s persistent state lives in a portable Ox Profile containing its identity, memory, skills, artifacts, and conversations. The goal is for that state to stay independent of any particular interface, including Ox itself, or model provider. File over app. The first implementation is an iOS app. It’s available on the App Store, and the whole thing is open source: https://openox.ai/ https://github.com/ziyzhu/openox If you’re interested in the broader motivation behind the project, I wrote about it here: https://ziyzhu.com/a-technology-for-free-will This is still early. I’m especially interested in feedback on the security model and self-evolution. I built Ox from scratch but many aspects of the project were heavily inspired by Pi/OpenClaw and the idea of malleable software. Ox’s core agent loop on iOS is pretty much a Swift rewrite of the Pi core package. Happy to answer anything about the implementation or protocol.

projects.title: Show HN: AgentRun: DSL to turn agents into workflows
projects.author: miguelrios

github.name: Parcha-ai/agentrun
github.description: The Agentrun Workflow DSL

projects.summary: Hi HN, I just open sourced the DSL that our harness in grep.ai uses to turn repeatable parts of agent work into workflows. You can combine tool calls, code, Jev-powered system one decisions for things like routing and screening evidence, and agents when a step needs more investigation. Our harness uses the traces and retro notes agents leave behind when doing a job to figure out which parts can become a workflow. The idea is to make the work easier to understand and avoid paying for a full agent loop where one isn’t needed. For example, a research workflow can split a question into subquestions, send agents to research them in parallel, use Jev to screen the evidence, and have another agent write the report. You can inspect the steps, evaluate the evidence screening separately, or change one agent without rebuilding everything. The DSL and examples are in our GitHub. There’s a scripted demo you can run without API keys: https://github.com/Parcha-ai/agentrun You can also use it as a Pi extension to build, inspect, and run workflows: https://github.com/Parcha-ai/agentrun#use-it-in-pi I would love to hear if this is useful to others. More background on how AgentRun works in this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vOVhtGjtwpg . Or read about our use cases in this article: https://x.com/MiguelriosEN/status/2101029313906987422 .

projects.title: Show HN: XHTML – Expert HTML
projects.author: plaguna
projects.summary: Hello everyone, I wanted to share with you one of my crazy ideas that I have been working on for the last couple of months. The platform is a collectible card platform, like Pokemon TCG, where you use your cards to build a website. Each day you get a new pack, with HTML tags, attributes, CSS elements, etc. and you have to make the most of those to compete against other devs. The idea is to figure out how to do more with less and to learn from others. As for some background on this... I have many crazy ideas, my brain can't stop sometimes. Using AI to write code for me has scratched some of the itches that my brain has farted through the years and have been living rent free in there for way too many years. Now they can land into the world (and maybe they shouldn't?) and I can free some mental space for new crazy ideas. I have develop my career in security (cybersecurity, couldn't hurt a fly even if I tried) and one common thing I saw when dealing with a free text field is that users could insert some HTML tags, but only from a shortlist. Things like <b> or <i> but never <script> or <video>. Well, my brain thought: "what if they add 1000000000e56 <b>s? Don't we want to limit that too?" and that thought has been in my head for too long. That is why, to test some of the AI coding capabilities, I created the html-allowlist npm package[0] early this year. Once I had that done my brain was happy and I was happy. A library that does what I always thought it was the best way of filtering content: you can add some flourish to your comment/textfield but not _too much_. Not sure if anyone will ever use it, but now they can. Then another thought came in: what is that make us scratch that pleasure of achieving more with less? With AI you have all that stream of code pouring without any effort but there was some pleasure on the struggles to get things to work when resources where limited or finding creative ways to do things on our own. As a bit of a gamer myself, quickly thought on the Pokemon TCG mobile app, where you get daily packs, build your deck and you battle. And because I have now the library that prevents more than N tags/elements to be present in an HTML page, I could apply that here and build something similar. So I did, I have been trying to apply all my learning from years of working as a security engineer in different companies to try and build a website that allows people to have a simple personal website but also showcase their web kung-fu skills. I was very happy when I saw a few days ago here about CSS Zen Garden[1] because this website was an early career inspiration for me, as well as being a type of scenario where I could see this platform going: small web mastercrafted by hand. I know people will come and say "if you didn't code it yourself why should we bother with it?" and you are more than welcome to do so. But for me this is about finally getting that idea out into the world, which maybe doesn't need a website like this, but maybe there's some joy on opening a random pack, slowly improving ones webpage, learning about an obscure CSS trick and appreciating others' skills. Anyway, I hope you give this a go, it is my first attempt to release something that feels, hopefully, like a final product, so happy to hear what you all have to say and see what you get to build. Pedro Laguna - https://pedro.laguna.es/ [0] https://www.npmjs.com/package/html-allowlist [1] https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49713262

projects.title: 【开源自荐】geo-sleuth：没有文字的照片，AI 也能找出拍摄地点
projects.author: Oldcircle

github.name: Oldcircle/geo-sleuth
github.description: An agent skill that finds where a photo was taken — OpenStreetMap geometry, elevation skylines, satellite imagery and street view — and shows its work. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and GitHub Copilot.

projects.summary: （MIT） geo-sleuth 是一个 Agent Skill。把一张照片交给 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 这类 agent，说一句「这张照片是在哪拍的」，它会给出拍摄机位、镜头朝向和一张卫星证据图。 它和让大模型直接看图猜地点不一样：模型只负责读画面、提线索，搜索和排序交给二十个 Python 脚本，用 OpenStreetMap 几何、高程数据、卫星图和街景去比对。所以画面里没有招牌、车牌、地标，也能往下查。 README 里的案例：一张抹掉 EXIF 的手机照片，稻田边一个白色烤炉，远处一条高架，右边一座山，没有一个字。 从 OpenStreetMap 取出区域内 27,335 段铁路桥，用高程算地平线，筛到 171 处 渲染 14,372 个候选机位的山脊线和照片比对，剩 3 个 把照片里 17 根桥墩当尺子，最后定到广东清远的一个点，误差约 2 米，全程约 72 分钟 安装： bash npx skills add Oldcircle/geo-sleuth

projects.title: Show HN: PlaceCall (YC W26) – agentic API to call businesses and get things done
projects.author: ymarkov
projects.summary: Hi HN, this is Yarik and Vlad from VOYGR - we are building the tools for agents and apps to engage with local businesses. It all started with our own pain point at VOYGR: calling businesses to verify if they are open. We are both from Google (Maps and Search) and even there, the merchants and venues don’t keep this info updated. So we built an API and started using it in-house. On July 4th, we were driving through Portland looking for a place to eat. Google Maps was saying “Holiday hours may vary”. We tried some AI assistant apps (Poke was trending back then), and they couldn’t help. Our API found 15 Thai and sushi places and called it in parallel. A few confirmed that they are open today and are taking walk-ins. One was marked closed on Google. The app can find the restaurant, but someone has to answer the phone. This is the problem we kept seeing. Assistants can’t do much in the real world where the phone number is still a major communication interface. Muse added calls in beta mode, but it’s still calling only one place at a time. There are a bunch of tools to create your own voice agents, but nothing that can work simply out of the box. We’ve built PlaceCall to fit all your agentic needs. Give it a task in plain English and a US phone number (or a list of numbers) - it navigates phone menus, waits for you on hold, and returns a structured response with outcome, recording and transcript. If you don’t have a phone number, just describe what you need and PlaceCall comes up with the recommendations. Here is the demo: https://youtu.be/7ZbVCPv8Wq0?si=LoLxxx1M7nhS7_j- When PlaceCall API was tested in our hackathon, we had the following use cases implemented by the developers: checking if a doctor accepts new patients, getting quotes for car service, and running quick surveys. The API can be used through Claude Code and Codex; examples and setup are listed in the repo: https://github.com/voygr-tech/placecall We give the first 250 calls free. Product page is here: https://voygr.tech/placecall/ Try it and let us know how it goes. We are interested in learning what you would use it for and what is missing. We are here all day and happy to answer any questions. Our email: founders@voygr.tech

projects.title: Show HN: HookDeploy – Webhook infra with mTLS private delivery
projects.author: mbernstein01
projects.summary: Hi HN! I'm Michael and I built HookDeploy. HookDeploy is a webhook infrastructure tool that captures webhooks at the edge, allows for inspection, transformation and fanout to multiple destinations including to your own private infrastructure with our first-party (source-available) mTLS agent. Runs as a service on Linux, lives in the tray on Windows and in the menu bar on Mac. As I'm sure most of you you have felt webhooks kind of suck if things don't go exactly as planned. Dropped webhooks or failures are likely silent. What actually drove me to build this was cleaning up after major cloud outages more than once. Cross referencing what System A knew against what System B actually had and reentering data by hand or trying to simulate events firing again. I have spent weeks of my life cleaning up webhook failures. HookDeploy solves that problem with a button and intelligent grouping of failed requests into incidents. If you've ever seen or had to clean up after a ransomware attack - you understand why I'd prefer to keep my firewall as tight as possible too. Our agent enables developers and teams to keep ports closed - if there is nothing to scan, there is nothing to attack. Getting to our own mTLS agent was a journey of trying to integrate existing solutions: first WireGuard (too much operational overhead), then Tailscale which was excellent, but it had real drawbacks on the required memory per joined tailnet and the additional cost to a user's Tailscale bill. It took several months to get it right, but it was worth every week of it. A few things to note at launch: we are launching with security measures in place: data is encrypted at rest with org-scoped keys rotated weekly (BYOK is on the roadmap), segregated databases for US, EU, APAC and AU so customer data stays where customers are not traversing underwater fiber to come to the US. We have 7 private delivery exit regions: San Francisco (us-west), New York (us-east), London (uk-london), Amsterdam (eu-west), Frankfurt (eu-central), Singapore (ap-southeast) and Sydney (au-southeast). Our platform is built primarily on Cloudflare for speed and security utilizing workers, KV, R2, Queues, Tunnels/VPC, and of course DNS and security. This has been some time in the making and I am excited to answer your questions and get feedback! Thank you in advance!

projects.title: Show HN: NetHackers
projects.author: vokneruk
projects.summary: hi everyone, been building this project for the last ~1.5 months (cc+superpowers all the way) it is an open effort to find a program that can reliably win NetHack 3.6.6: you can write a bot by hand, let claude code / codex / opencode improve one, or build your own harness that improves the thing that improves the bot me and my lab switched to the goal-based research this year (we worked a lot in the idea-based framework for a last couple of years) -- and decided that we would like to tackle the NetHack, it is one of those nasty roguelike that is still somehow not solved with all fancy AI models (yes, even astra) -- probably on the way something useful will appear you can pull someone else's bot, run experiments locally and register the results. every registered program is linked to your github repo and exact source commit i always wanted to try building something that will use github as both social and storage layer (and it seems to work quite well in our case, simplified things a bit and i think this approach is quite cool) there is a shared frontier across 73 starting identities -- your bots dont have to be the best at everything to contribute something useful, e.g. if you love to roleplay gnomes only, so be it to make thing easier (for both harness devs and people who are just playing around), we provide a loop that does some sort of an evolutionary optimization process (quality-diversity, etc), ofc you don't have to use it. but you can start with in minutes (given you have codex or claude subs) you can also bring your own search, your own harness, whatever -- the common ground is the evaluation. public seeds are there for people to overfit (in nethack even overfitting is hard), and we separately re-evaluate on hidden seeds to check whether the improvements actually transfer one of my goals was to actually try to make it at least a bit fun -- hope you enjoy the web-site and easter eggs

projects.title: Show HN: Groupicorn directory of IOP group therapy programs
projects.author: cs1996
projects.summary: Hello fellow tech workers! My name is Andrew, cs major from University of Pittsburgh 1996 and long time BBS SysOp from 1991-1993. I grew up chatting online as a teenager. Before this new fangled internet came around, back in my day, ok sorry, to the point: Isolation and work from home jobs can drive you a little crazy. It was always my dream before 2020. Getting the powers that be to agree to work from home. Now six years later it's definitely a careful what you wish for type situation. I got to a point with just code code code all day, interacting with no humans that I broke. Where do humans go for repair? I didn't really know. Turns out there's something called an IOP (intensive outpatient program) and yes it has the word "intensive" right in the title. Is it intense? <robert de nero voice>little bit</rdnv> But also wonderful. All of a sudden I had a place to go Monday thru Friday and co-workers / friends! In fact, it was even better than previous office jobs because we didn't just sit next to each other on laptops and not talk, this was group therapy. I was never a fan of individual one-on-one talk therapy. But wow, group therapy is something very different. Therapists can be incredibly helpful. Doctors can be incredibly helpful. They've spent years learning things I haven't. But they're also human. We're all flawed humans. The really interesting thing about a group is that suddenly the wisdom doesn't have to come from one person it can come from fifteen. Somebody half your age says something and you think, "OMG. They're completely right." Somebody talks about a problem that's nothing like yours, and somehow they describe exactly what you've been feeling for the last ten years. Sometimes you see somebody else describing the same ridiculous thing you've been doing, and it's much easier to recognize it when somebody ELSE does it. Sometimes the person running the group says the thing that sticks with you. Sometimes it's the guy sitting next to you eating a granola bar. There's wisdom in the group. The site is all about helping people find, tour and enroll in your first IOP programs. https://groupicorn.com/ https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JhoAHUU2TCM https://github.com/groupicorn/list-of-programs Open source system to find all the programs in every state. We have iphone and android app mobile apps as well. Feedback much appreciated.

projects.summary: I built Ceptile because I wanted a search tool that could combine the convenience of an AI answer with the ability to inspect the actual web pages behind it. A Ceptile search retrieves pages from the web, ranks the retrieved sources, and uses them to produce an answer with links back to the sources. I've also been building some things around the search workflow, including Notes for keeping research, translation tools, and ways to work with information found during a search. A lot of the work so far has been figuring out the search pipeline itself: retrieving useful pages, dealing with noisy results, deciding which sources should be used, and keeping the connection between an answer and its sources. I'm particularly interested in where the current system breaks down. For example, if you try it with a query that you already know well, I'd be interested in whether the retrieved sources are useful and whether the citations make it easy to verify the answer. https://ceptile.com/ Watch 2 minutes demo on Youtube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OR4WfsMKEiE Join Our Discord Server on: https://discord.gg/N9wRwBTDD

projects.title: Show HN: Parametric, low-poly assets for BIM/CAD
projects.author: matt3D
projects.summary: I've been learning and working in the 3D CAD/BIM space for almost 20 years and one thing that often comes up is the availability of simple assets that are efficiently modelled. One of the challenges I see a lot is an Architect will need to model a kitchen unit, so they go to BIM Object or another library and download a model. There are two problems this creates; firstly the 3D element itself contains an enormous number or polygons which can cause performance issues, and second the Architect is at risk of over-specifying that particular unit when really they just wanted it as a placeholder. So I built 3DAssetStudio.com to alleviate some of that, I've been slowly picking through the various different categories of assets that might be needed and ended up with over 500 core types, which have 4,000+ presets, which can be adjusted parametrically into millions of combinations. I used FreeCAD script and then built a compiler, so now I can add new elements quite quickly, and the URL parameters configure the asset, so sharing or bookmarking models is really easy. I'm not sure what to do next, for now I've set a 20 models/week download limit just in case I find a commercial strategy that works, but it's all open to play around with without signing up.

projects.title: Show HN: Lightdrift / Image search for AI agents through API and MCP
projects.author: jacksonholland
projects.summary: Greetings HN, I'm Jackson, the founder of Lightdrift. It's an image search API and MCP that lets agents retrieve real images, along with natural language descriptions, metadata, provenance, and license conditions. I built this because I kept having the same problem and it was pissing me off. About a year ago, I was vibe coding on edibles. I decided to build a pipeline that generated educational, short form videos about marine biology, because I was watching Planet Earth but I was being distracted by reels, and I needed comfort. I realized video generation struggled with less familiar animals, like the Mola Mola, which is my favorite marine animal because idk there is just something about it that is relatable. Naturally, I decided I would just ground the videos by retrieving images automatically. I realized the existing APIs for this had meh developer experiences, and instantly gave up lol. Later, I was building an AI education platform. I wanted lessons to include relevant visuals, but generated images weren't consistently reliable for actual species, people, places, etc. Again, I needed image retrieval, and I made a shitty aggregration of APIs and wrappers that ended up becoming the entire project. I tried Unsplash, Pexels, Brave search, Exa, my own wrappers around Wikimedia Commons. Each helped with part of the problem. Stock libraries worked for broad subjects but didn't consistenly cover the specific things my applications needed. Web search helped locate material, but I still had to resolve the image files, check their sources and usage conditions, and turn inconsistent results into something the application could consume. I wrapped Commons which again left me handling search quality and normalization myself. The goal of Lightdrift is to bring that tedious ass work into one place. We source, caption, index, and host the images. An app/agent can search in natural language and receive image giles with the context needed to select and use them. The corpus currently contains over two million diverse images, pretty much entirely CC and public domain material. The license info describes the source's stated permissions/conditions. It isn't a blanket guarantee that every image can be used, but it always gives the information you/your agent need to decide. I think (know) this could be applied to education tools, presentation builders, and app builders that need relevant imagery without maintaining a separate image pipeline. I'm currently looking for design partners (but also it's super easy to set up so we don't have to make it official lol). If your application needs particular subjects that we don't cover well, I will work with you to source and index it at no additional cost. Does image retrieval currently break down in what you're building? Product: https://lightdrift.ai Docs: https://docs.lightdrift.ai

projects.title: Show HN: flyOS – A fruit fly connectome simulated in real time on an iPhone
projects.author: coryetzkorn
projects.summary: Hey HN, I'm Cory. When I saw Google release the fruit fly connectome, I wanted to experiment with it myself and better understand how the fruit fly brain works, so I started hacking on a few different iOS projects. Originally I was going to create an app that let you experience BEING a fruit fly with VR, but then I realized that a fruit fly's main sense is its smell, and an iPhone can't smell. So I ended up building an app based on all of the senses an iPhone has that we could wire to a fruit fly. I came up with flyOS: basically the camera is its eyes, the CPU is its brain, etc. The neuron simulator is written from scratch in Swift and runs in real time on the phone's CPU, with no server involved. Yes, this is partly a joke. But it's also a serious app that lets you view the neurons of a simulated fly in real time, which I think is pretty cool. I wrote a white paper and put it online to share the process of building this, and why I ultimately only ended up using 4,895 neurons out of the total 166,000 in the release. Would love your feedback and thoughts as to how I could make the fly even more realistic and alive.

projects.title: [开源推荐] 每条规则都注明典籍出处的东方术数计算库
projects.author: zaoxu001

github.name: zaoxu001/tianzhi-core
github.description: 东方术数的核心算法：以典籍为据，把可推算的部分还原成可检验的算法

projects.summary: 术数里真正属于推算的那一部分——干支纪时、排盘、五行力量量化、旺衰分档、调候取用、月令格局、岁运引动、合盘——本来是有规则、有出处、可复现的。但公开实现大多只给结论不说依据，同一张盘换个库结果就不一样，用的人无从查证。 tianzhi-core 把这部分做成纯函数库：输入出生时刻与经度，输出结构化数据与术语标签，不做文字解读。有出处的规则在代码里注明篇名，无法从典籍直接推出的系数标注为本包取值、可调整。历法层直接采用 lunar-python，不作重复实现。 目前八字一门做得完整（排盘、排运、量化、取用、引动、合盘、神煞），其余门类在同一套底座上陆续展开。 pip install tianzhi-core，Python 3.10+，MIT 许可。 亮点 1. 口径可查。 《穷通宝鉴》《子平真诠》《神峰通考》《滴天髓》《金不换大运》的篇名在代码注释里出现 43 处。某条判据出自哪一部书的哪一篇，可以对着原文逐条印证。无法从典籍直接推出的工程系数单独标注为本包取值，与有出处的规则区分开。 2. 流派分歧做成显式参数，不替使用者选边。 例如晚子时（23:00–23:59）的日柱算哪一天，两派相争且各有依据——本包给 latezi 参数，两派都实现，默认值在注释里附理由。同类的还有阳刃是否给阴干、取用以格局为先还是调候为先。 3. 纯函数。 不读系统时间，不访问网络与文件系统（包内数据表除外），同一输入永远得到同一输出，跨进程一致。181 个测试锁住已确定的口径，改动时不会把旧结论悄然回退。 4. 分层清楚，改哪一层一目了然。 calendar 历法（真太阳时、节气时刻，属天文计算，只有对错）/ core 干支五行（基础常识，其上所有逻辑依赖于此）/ bazi 旺衰调候格局取用（口径分歧集中于此层，也最欢迎讨论）。

projects.title: Show HN: Combinators in Array Languages
projects.author: softwarewright
projects.summary: Raymond Smullyan’s "To Mock a Mockingbird" book's aviary of combinator birds implemented in APL-derived languages and the problem implementing the Sage bird (Fixed Point or Y combinator) in an eagerly evaluated language. Newer APLs support lazy evaluation. My eager language has a workaround for this. The Z combinator is the standard strict-language fix: wrap the self-application in one extra function layer (λv. x x v), so the recursion is a value (a delayed call) rather than an executing expression. sw-MLPL expresses that delay as a named partial — z_step/z_recur/applicative_sage — because the language has no anonymous lambdas. Z has no Smullyan name (and no zebra in the aviary, despite the letter). The book predates and ignores the strictness problem, so it has no applicative-order variant. "Z combinator" is programmer folklore for the eta-expanded Y

projects.title: Show HN: Kado – Search to Allow Personal Agents to Find Agent Apps
projects.author: vaishnavsm
projects.summary: Hey folks! My cofounder and I have built Kado - Search for Personal Agents to find Agent Apps[1]. We think the future of agents that individuals will use few personal agents (think, personal computers) as their primary interface, and while those agents delegate work to agent apps to complete actual tasks. We were building a personal agent ourselves when we noticed that our users were often trying to do complex things which should be delegated away. We found that web search didn't cut it for reasons including the "quality metric" being incorrect, and a "don't know what to search for" problem. Kado's crawl uses LLMs to parse information from websites pages, agent cards, or other discovery sources to model the actual outcome(s) that's being promised, and the interface to them (we call these "agent apps"). Our search and index is based on a heavily modified version of HyDE. The search itself is quite slow right now because of LLMs in the loop. We want to get this down to ~sub-second. We have ~3000 indexed MCPs and/or A2A agents, and we recently purged the index of entries your agents can't use (we had ~45k before that). I'm partial to a TTRPG character generator MCP that's great for printed one shot sheets, but some others you may also want to try searching for include builder/research/crawl tools or (surprisingly) financial data tools. Also, did you know that AWS has a public devops/root cause analysis agent?[2] The best way to try it is to install it on your agent (it's a CLI + Skill for now, MCP coming soon!) but you can also just try direct searches on the website. The website requires a google login for spam protection (which we want to remove if we get some funding haha), but the CLI does not need a login (we use proof of work to prevent spam, and an agent identity based on a keypair is auto-created and stored in your keychain). Would love any feedback! PS: Ignore the order of the search results - our experiments show that the ranking does not matter for intelligent models, so we've prioritized recall over ranking. [1] https://kado.so and https://kado.so/about [2] AWS DevOps Agent - https://connect.aidevops.us-east-1.api.aws/.well-known/agent...

projects.title: Show HN: DrivingBench – Frontier LLMs Driving a Real Toyota Corolla
projects.author: aditya-ramabadr
projects.summary: Hi all, wanted to share a cool project me and two buddies have been working on. Essentially we took a Toyota Corolla, installed a Comma 4, hooked it up to GPT-6 Astra/Claude Fable/Grok 4.6/Sol, gave them MCP tools to control the Toyota, and then we let them try driving a cone course (in an empty parking lot at low speed). They can observe the cameras/telemetry, request steering/speed, and stop the car. The goal was to see how good frontier LLMs might be just out-of-the-box at a task like driving a real physical car (inspired by recent such demos in robotics). The best model was GPT-6 Astra which fully finished the course on its second attempt (which was pretty shocking to us). We gave each model up to 3 attempts on the course in the same chat conversation (to incentivize in-context learning). Fable also improved quite a bit from 9% to 45% by its 3rd attempt. We also have a trace viewer at our website (for example see https://drivingbench.com/trace/gpt-6-astra/2/ for Astra's successful attempt), and everything is open source (traces, harness/code at https://github.com/aditya-ramabadran/drivingbench_harness_v1 , we have a report at https://drivingbench.com/report/ on how we did everything, some of the things that went wrong or that we could do better, etc). Obvious disclaimer: the models clearly aren't good enough to drive on an actual road yet. Also we did this at super low speeds in an open parking lot with a human always ready to brake at any time. Please use the harness/code/etc at your own risk. Would love to answer any questions or take any feedback for v2!

projects.title: Show HN: WebGCM – a global climate model running in the browser on WebGPU
projects.author: jlhawn
projects.summary: I started this four and a half years ago. I wanted to build a climate model as both a toy and educational tool that I could visualize in a web browser. I have always been interested in meteorology and asked r/ClimateScience for advice on the math and physics on building an in-browser climate model as an educational tool, and a few people said it was far too ambitious. They were right. I could build the geometry, an icosahedral hexagonal grid on a globe, and I have an intuitive understanding of the math but integrating the Navier-Stokes equations and the physics proved to be too difficult for me, and the closest I got after nearly of month of work was a model that blew up within two simulated days. Fast forward 4 and a half years. I figured that if models like Claude and GPT Astra could solve a milennium prize problem about fluid dynamics then they could help me fix the broken model and iterate on it until my vision was realized. On Friday, I threw down $200 for a Claude Max subscription, and this is the result of a single weekend's work on top of where I had left off. What it is now, in technical terms: a hydrostatic primitive-equation atmosphere on that hex grid (the TRiSK scheme MPAS uses), 27 levels, about 41,000 cells at 110 km, with grey radiation, moist convection, a boundary layer, sea ice, a land surface with snow, a two-layer ocean and real topography. Every kernel runs on the GPU; on my MacBook Pro (M1 Max) it does about 70 simulated hours a minute from a six-year spin-up, hence the 50 MB first load. You can color the globe by twenty-odd fields, animate wind or currents, draw isobars, or view it from space under the model's own sun. The URL captures the view, so links open specific places. Caveats: an educational model, not a validated one. It runs about four degrees colder than Earth and I'm still tuning it, the ocean is crude and shallow, and it needs WebGPU (Chrome, Edge, Safari 26) for best performance. It's currently tuned for my specific machine specs but I suspect it will run well on most desktop-class Apple Silicon machines from the past 5 years. Source and design notes: https://github.com/jlhawn/geodesic Edit: If it runs really well on your machine, something well above 100 simulated hours per minute (displayed on the top-left of the page), let me know your machine specs! You should also try to reload the page with `?N=128` in the query params and it will re-grid to an even higher resolution. But it will take a few simulated days to settle down after the initial shock from the changed resolution. If you end up tyring this, check out the Temperature overlay at 10 hPa height and you should see Gravity Waves [1] rippling through the top of the atmosphere! [1] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gravity_wave

projects.author: dwa3592
projects.summary: Jev's launch inspired me to work on this project. I had used fine tuned bert models, zero-shot models to achieve jev like functionality in healthcare insurance fraud audits in the last 2-3 years with good results. Jev's launch showed that there is still market and demand for these type of systems. So I wanted to build a FOSS version which would push the research and tinkering (R&T) in this direction. Do not use this where decisions can be costly. There's an accuracy/intelligence ceiling with these models no matter what the api seller tells you. Use this where you can tell the affected party - "oh yeah, sometimes it can mess up" and you both can have a laugh on the expense of machines. On Jev and Typesafe - I think Jev is great, especially the speed, the documentation and the product design itself. Happy to answer any questions. Thanks, D

projects.title: Show HN: Mathy – Build Math Automaticity
projects.author: gmays
projects.summary: Mathy is a free tool I made to build math automaticity. If you think of something like Anki for drilling problems/formulas, it's like that but built for math and more convenient: no creating your own cards, it works well on mobile and helps track your progress over time. It uses FSRS for scheduling and includes over 40,000 problems ranging from 1st grade math through university level math, all deterministically verified. It also has levels and dozens of badges you can earn to keep it engaging. You can use it via the iOS app or the web app. The iOS app is free and completely offline aside from optionally sending feedback/requesting help in app. In the web version progress is stored locally in IndexedDB, except in challenge mode where you can optionally submit initials to the leaderboard. I still use Math Academy to learn math (highly recommended), but as I'm learning more advanced math to support my journey into AI and robotics I wanted to try and raise my own ceiling by building automaticity in stuff I already learned. The idea is a little counterintuitive: if Mathy works, you should eventually need it less. Because as something becomes automatic, its recommended reviews can move farther apart thanks to FSRS. Edit: More about how I made it here https://gmays.com/making-math-automatic-with-mathy/

projects.title: Show HN: Mini-AGI – Dynamic continual learning model trained on 8GB VRAM
projects.author: volotat

github.name: volotat/mini-AGI
github.description: Continual learning model trained from scratch on 8GB VRAM laptop with batch-1 stream of data.

projects.summary: Sorry for the pretentious name, I know, I know.. It just contains all the pieces I would like to see a AGI model to have, and I can't stand the temptation. Before throwing rocks at me, please take a glance at the Readme, and I hope it will cover your mood a little bit. So, first of all it does work and you can see the sample from the whole training run here: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/volotat/mini-AGI/refs/head... Here is the scaling law graph I have so far, and it looks very promising: https://github.com/volotat/mini-AGI/blob/main/assets/scaling... The model was built under my deep dissatisfaction so we cannot really train even moderately big models (1B+ scale) on the consumer's hardware. We can inference and fine-tune them for sure, but I would like to have full control over what the model sees over the training run, so it is fully aligned with my interests, not some corporations. I was thinking about for some time and come up with two interesting ideas I thought worth pursuing: MoE with a lot of experts that gets added and pruned from the model while it trains, where only a small subset of of experts are actually in use at any particular moment + batch 1 training on the single continuous stream of data. First allows us to be bounded only by the disk space in terms of number of parameters and load and unload experts only when they are needed. The second (if figured out and it turns out to be doable) allows us to get aways with small VRAM capacity because we do not need to store big randomized batches and their respective gradients. I started brainstorming with Claude and after some time we found an approach that seems to be promising, and low and behold, a few weeks pass and you can see the results yourself. Obviously, I did use AI in the process of making this project and I am pretty sure it would be completely impossible for me to do something like this without it, so I hope it is more than justified. The model is still running over the first of 7.8B characters corpus I selected for training, so the weights are not out yet, and it's about a couple weeks of waiting until they are cooked at the current reading speed. And yeah, the model just read continuous interleaved passages from the dataset, each by 32K characters long each as a single stream. Just as you or I would do. The set up seems to be really simple so you can git clone the project, run it and observe everything for yourself. Thanks for your attention.

projects.summary: 英文入口： 大家好，自荐一个正在维护的网站项目 EasyDomain。它想解决的问题是：找到一个网站后，除了点开使用，也能更方便地了解它做什么、寻找同类工具，并查看相关的域名与技术资料。 目前可以： 按分类、标签和关键词查找网站，继续浏览相关网站。 在详情页查看网站介绍、截图，以及可获取的 DNS、HTTPS 证书、邮件服务、技术栈和社交分享信息。 使用 DNS、HTTPS 等查询入口，配合站内知识文章理解这些信息。 例如，挑选在线工具时可以先从标签找到候选，再看详情和同类网站；排查某个域名的配置时，则可以从查询工具进入对应资料。网站可直接浏览，无需注册。 目前仍在持续完善分类和数据质量；技术信息展示的是采集时的情况，不是安全背书，部分介绍与问答由 AI 辅助生成。欢迎反馈实际使用中遇到的分类、检索和信息展示问题。 这是一则项目方自荐，感谢周刊提供资源投稿入口。

projects.author: IRONICBo

github.name: socai-io/jev-social
github.description: Jev-powered Instagram, TikTok, and LinkedIn research: typed routing, real browser evidence, streamed post cards, video capture, and cited socai reports.

projects.summary: Jev Social 是一个本地优先的社交媒体研究 Agent。它让 Jev 从动态操作列表中逐步选择搜索、打开帖子或评论、下载视频和结束研究，再由 socai CLI 在用户已登录的 Chrome 中执行。适合追踪 Instagram、TikTok 与 LinkedIn 话题，并输出可回查来源的帖子卡片和研究报告。 亮点 Jev 真正参与每一步，而不只判断一次平台：每轮候选操作都来自上一步抓到的具体帖子、用户与 URL；Jev 决定下一条只读操作，执行结果再回到下一轮判断。 模型不生成选择器或 shell 命令：Jev 只能从程序给出的类型化操作空间中选择，socai CLI 负责真实页面的导航、滚动和结构化提取，降低任意浏览器操作的风险。 证据先于总结：帖子、评论、视频和来源链接边抓边显示，最后的报告引用已捕获内容；登录门槛、限流或步数耗尽时返回诚实的部分结果，不伪装成功。 本地优先：复用用户本机 Chrome 的登录状态，不依赖远程云浏览器。两条 npx 命令即可完成引导并启动界面。 项目采用 MIT 许可证，提供 53 个自动化测试、GitHub Actions、贡献与安全说明。

projects.title: 做了一个面向 AI Agent 的开源文档解析与检索系统，方便做工程和金融 agent 的老哥
projects.author: cs1707
projects.summary: 之前做了一个解析+记忆的小工具 Knowhere ，很多人都觉得跟 MinerU 有点像，其实 MinerU 只负责解析，Knowhere 还会把解析之后的 chunking 、embedding 一系列事情都做了，直接变成 AI agent 可以直接调用、检索、回溯、查找的记忆层。Knowhere 更偏现实场景一点，因为一开始弄这个项目，就是因为现实场景的文档太脏，普通解析更多面向办公场景的资料，对现实场景的脏文档解析效果不佳。 现在 Knowhere 又更新了一版，新增了一条纯视觉解析路线——vision-map ，更好地服务那些不便转化成文档的资料了。欢迎大家来试试： https://knowhereto.ai/github/?utm_source=v2ex 简单讲一下使用的场景。一份排版清晰的 Word 文档，转换成结构化文本以后，标题、段落和表格通常都能被准确保留下来。但如果面对的是扫描合同、复杂研报、演示文稿或者工程图纸，情况就不一样了。 这些文件中的信息不只存在于文字里，还存在于页面布局、表格关系、图形位置、颜色、标注和相邻内容之间。传统解析一旦读错顺序、漏掉数字或者拆散表格，错误就可能被写进知识库，并在之后被 Agent 反复使用。 VISION-MAP 采用了另一种思路：不急着把页面完全改写成文字，而是保留原始页面，让视觉模型从整个页面出发理解内容。系统会为页面建立章节归属、主题说明和必要的内容标注，再把它组织进文档地图。Agent 需要时，可以先找到相关页面，再直接查看原页。 到了 Knowhere 2.0 ，这条视觉路线与原有的文本解析组成了一套双轨架构。文本轨负责高效地读 Word 、Excel 、Markdown 、JSON 等结构比较清晰的资料，Knowhere 会尽可能保留准确的文字和原生结构。视觉轨负责完整地看 PDF 、PPT 等以页面为主要载体的文档，Knowhere 2.0 可以通过视觉模型理解完整页面，所以不需要转化成 Markdown ，直接保留原页面进入搜索。 两条轨道最终会进入同一套文档记忆。 对 Agent 来说，文本段落和视觉页面都会被组织成带有章节层级、来源位置、相关资产和文档关系的节点。Agent 可以在同一个知识库里查找它们，也可以在一次任务中同时读取文字和页面。 这给用户带来了几个直接变化： - 不必为了建立知识库，先把所有资料手动转换成同一种格式； - 干净文档依然可以使用高效、准确的文本解析； - 图纸、扫描件和复杂报告不再因为难以完美转写而被挡在知识库之外； - Agent 给出结论后，可以继续回到具体章节、页码和原始页面进行核验。 此外，Knowhere 2.0 还更新了 Agent 原生检索。上一个版本中，MapNav 已经开始利用文档结构进行导航，但它仍然是一套相对固定的检索流程。每个问题大致沿着预设路径完成查找，Agent 能够使用的策略仍然有限。 Knowhere 2.0 则进一步把这套能力开放成 Agent 可以自主使用的文档记忆底座。 系统会向 Agent 提供文档大纲、章节结构、精确搜索、模糊召回、全文阅读、图片和表格资产，以及跨文档关系等工具。至于先调用哪一个工具、以什么顺序调用、需要深入到哪一层，由 Agent 根据当前任务自己判断。 面对一个简单问题，Agent 可以直接搜索并返回答案。 面对一个复杂问题，它也可以先查看有哪些资料，再阅读相关文档的目录；找到可能相关的章节后继续向下查找，读取完整段落或者原始页面；如果证据不足，还可以转向其他文档，比较不同版本，或者顺着相关实体继续探索。 整个过程更接近一个人在资料库中的真实工作方式： 1. 先了解资料范围； 2. 判断答案可能出现在哪里； 3. 沿着目录和线索缩小范围； 4. 阅读相关段落、页面和资产； 5. 对照其他文档补充或验证； 6. 带着文档、章节和页码返回结论。 由此，Agent 获得了调整检索策略的能力，如果第一次没有找到足够证据，它可以换一种工具或者继续向下阅读；如果问题涉及多个文档，它可以主动建立联系；如果用户继续追问，它也不必每次都从几个孤立片段重新开始。 结果显示，相比直接使用原始文档，Agent 使用 Knowhere 后的首次回答准确率提高了 36%，召回率提高了 11%；加入用户反馈后，准确率达到 79%，而直接读取原始文档的结果约为 53%。 除了准确率，Agent 完成任务所需的循环次数、时间和 Token 使用量也有所下降。原因并不是 Agent “读得更快”了，而是它可以沿着已经建立好的文档结构寻找答案，不必反复通读大段无关内容。 ![]( https://i.imgur.com/4D1JKev.png) 如果你也在做工程类知识库、企业尽调与制度核验这种直面现实场景的业务，那欢迎来试试。有什么问题，也欢迎反馈~ Knowhere：： https://knowhereto.ai/github/?utm_source=v2ex

projects.author: 0verme

github.name: 0verme/data-warehouse-visualized
github.description: 面向中文学习者的交互式数据仓库可视化教材，用图解、动画和模拟器理解数仓分层、建模、指标、调度、血缘、数据质量与湖仓。

projects.summary: 大家好，我做了一个中文交互式学习网站「数据仓库图解」，想向周刊自荐。 同一笔余额，为什么做一次 JOIN 就被算了三遍？两张报表都写着“存款余额”，为什么数字对不上？调度任务明明成功了，数据为什么还不能发布？ 这个项目尝试通过可操作的小型实验，把这些数据工程问题讲清楚。案例主要围绕银行账户、交易和余额展开，使用简化的教学数据，在浏览器里就能体验，无需安装数据库或大数据环境。 可以先试这三个实验： JOIN 为什么会让金额变大？：逐行观察匹配如何复制记录，以及调整粒度后结果怎样变化。 存款余额指标实验：切换统计范围，观察哪些账户被计入，以及指标结果为什么不同。 调度运行模拟器：观察上游迟到、任务失败和重跑如何影响下游。 适合刚接触数据仓库的同学，以及已经会写 SQL、想进一步理解数据加工链路的开发者。课程还涉及数据质量、血缘、湖仓和数据交付等主题。 项目还在持续完善，实验对生产场景做了教学简化。欢迎指出不准确的地方，也欢迎补充更容易讲清问题的案例。

projects.title: Show HN: Prohibition of Nuclear Launch Automation
projects.author: healthworker
projects.summary: I helped advocate for the following language in the annual US military funding bill from last year. Not very many people are aware that this is part of Federal law: it prohibits nuclear launch automation and requires a human in the loop for nuclear weapons employment. FY2025 NDAA SEC. 1638. SENSE OF CONGRESS WITH RESPECT TO USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TO SUPPORT STRATEGIC DETERRENCE. (a) Sense of Congress.—It is the sense of Congress that— (1) the considered use of artificial intelligence and machine learning tools presents opportunities to strengthen the security of critical strategic communications and early warning networks, improve the efficiency of planning processes to reduce the risk of collateral damage, and enhance U.S. capabilities for modeling weapons functionality in support of stockpile stewardship; and (2) even with such applications, particular care must be taken to ensure that the incorporation of artificial intelligence and machine learning tools does not increase the risk that our Nation’s most critical strategic assets can be compromised. (b) Statement of Policy.—It is the policy of the United States that the use of artificial intelligence efforts should not compromise the integrity of nuclear safeguards, whether through the functionality of weapons systems, the validation of communications from command authorities, or the principle of requiring positive human actions in execution of decisions by the President with respect to the employment of nuclear weapons.

projects.author: tronghieu

github.name: tronghieu/agent-skills
github.description: Method-driven agent skills for knowledge work: strategy, research, critical thinking, data analysis, docs, slides. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and any agentskills.io-compatible agent.

projects.summary: 目前大多数 Agent Skills 是给程序员写代码用的。这个仓库里的 18 个 skill 面向做决策、做研究、写文档的人：设计思维、批判性思考、根因分析、市场调研、战略分析、数据分析、长文档精读、Diataxis 文档写作、演示文稿等。 我是越南的开发者，这些 skill 最初都是为自己的工作写的，现在仍在日常使用。 特点 每个 skill 是一套带步骤和检查点的方法。以 design-thinking 为例：每条洞察必须能追溯到登记过的证据来源，没有来源的结论会一直标注为"假设"；到了用户访谈环节，agent 会停下来等你去做真实访谈，不会编造用户画像和引语。 deep-reader 用于精读 50 页以上的书、论文或学位论文，不需要把全文塞进上下文，并保留带页码的笔记，下次可以接着提问。 遵循 agentskills.io 的 SKILL.md 规范。我自己在 Claude 和 DeepSeek 模型上实际使用过；Qwen Code、Kimi CLI、Trae 等工具也支持该规范，但我还没有逐一测试，欢迎反馈。 MIT 协议；仓库和每个 skill 都有中文 README。 安装 bash npx skills add tronghieu/agent-skills 只装一个 npx skills add tronghieu/agent-skills --skill deep-reader 如果访问 GitHub 较慢，skills/ 目录下每个 skill 都有对应的 zip 包，下载后解压到 ~/.claude/skills/ 或 ~/.agents/skills/ 即可。

projects.title: Jev Visual
projects.author: haoran

github.name: hr98w/jev-visual
github.description: An educational Jev-like visual inference experiment on Apple Silicon: shared context, direct candidate scoring, and local visual demos.

projects.summary: **Jev Visual** 是一个面向 Apple Silicon 的开源视觉推理实验项目，尝试用开放权重视觉语言模型复现一种 **Jev-like 的视觉决策范式**。 项目基于 **Qwen3.5-0.8B + MLX**，核心思路不是让模型针对每个问题分别进行自回归生成，而是： > **图像 + 公共上下文 → 一次 Prefill → 复用模型状态 → 批量处理多个问题 → 直接从 logits 对候选答案打分** 例如，同一张图片需要同时判断物体类别、位置、状态等几十个问题时，可以复用视觉编码和公共上下文，而不是重复处理整张图片。 项目目前支持： * **多选、Yes/No、等级评分**等结构化视觉决策 * 单张图片最多批量处理 **64 个问题** * 基于 **KV / recurrent state 复用**的 shared-prefix 推理 * 直接计算候选答案的 **log probability** * 本地 **Web UI、CLI 和 HTTP API** * 完全运行在 **Apple Silicon + MLX** 上，无需云端 GPU 为了验证这种推理方式，我还实现了几个实时视觉 Demo，包括 **AI 分拣工厂、视觉控制打砖块、摄像头手势识别**等。 在 M4 / 16GB Mac 上的实验中，当一次处理 64 个视觉决策时，独立候选评分耗时约 **37.3 秒**，共享上下文后的批量评分约 **2.4 秒**。这个 Benchmark 主要用于验证 shared-context 推理的扩展性，并不代表模型准确率提升。 这个项目并不是 TypeSafe Jev 官方模型的复现，也没有复现其 RLCD 训练、校准或 Serving 系统，而是一个基于开放模型探索 **“视觉模型是否一定需要通过生成来完成决策”** 的工程实验。
projects.summaryZh: 面向 Apple Silicon 的开源视觉推理实验，基于 Qwen3.5-0.8B + MLX。
projects.summaryEn: Apple Silicon visual reasoning experiment with Qwen3.5-0.8B + MLX. It reuses one prefill and KV state to score candidate answers from logits, batching up to 64 visual decisions per image, with local Web UI, CLI and HTTP API.

projects.title: Show HN: Scry, programmable internet search w/ congestion pricing
projects.author: Xyra
projects.summary: Meet Scry, a 500 TB NVMe internet index in ClickHouse that you can run ~arbitrary readonly SQL and some of Datalog over, and I handle the problem of resource-contention with congestion-based micro-auction pricing. When there's capacity, the service is free for non-commercial use. --- Hello. It's 2026, we're training simulated fruit fly brains to play Beat Saber, do we still have to be stuck with internet (re)search as fn: natural language -> black box we can't do anything about -> ranked_list/summary? There is a long history of people trying to do very fancy things that end up being done in relational databases and a little SQL. There is a gravity to them, a bitter lesson, just like scaling of generalized ml training methods. I mean many, many information products can be built off essentially giant real-time OLAP databases and frontier LLMs writing brilliant SQL+Datalog+vector+Jev etc. queries. Google Search, Tavily, Exa essentially have the problem of mapping your agents' context you are willing to provide, to a tiny subset of their index. You pay a fixed cost to an extremely hard problem that has a distribution of hardness, which means YOU eat the downsides when they are running out of budgeted compute to help you out. Their algorithms are opaque to the caller, there's really not much user control, and there's not a serious opportunity to communally improve search recipes, like the lexical+Jev recipes you trust to select bleeding edge AI builders. Furthermore, search companies aren't even pursuing text-to-SQL anymore (several have talked to me)... they made up their minds during the traumatic 2024 text-to-sql days. They were just too early. I hope you enjoy. I'm intent on scaling this paradigm on differentiated hardware over much more data, so any compelling use cases or queries I could show off, would be much appreciated!

Instead of static lessons or tedious quizzes, you step into realistic scenarios, question AI-powered roles, uncover missing evidence, challenge assumptions, and get feedback on how you reason.
projects.titleZh: Persona — How Well Do You Really Think?
projects.summaryZh: 通过真实场景训练批判性思维，质疑AI角色、发现缺失证据并挑战假设，获得推理反馈。
projects.titleEn: Persona — How Well Do You Really Think?
projects.summaryEn: AI can give you answers instantly. Persona trains the skill that matters next: deciding whether those answers, and the evidence behind them, deserve your trust.

projects.title: HuAI : Contests For Agents
projects.summary: HuAI is a competition arena for AI agents. Give agents the same research challenge, watch them submit evidence-backed answers, and let GPT-6 Astra judge their work against a published rubric. Inspect criterion scores and explanations to understand each result. For agent builders who want to see what their agents can actually do.
projects.summaryZh: 面向 AI Agent 的竞赛竞技场：让多个 Agent 解答同一研究挑战，由 GPT-6 Astra 按公开评分标准评判，并展示各项得分与解释。
projects.summaryEn: HuAI is a competition arena for AI agents. Give agents the same research challenge, watch them submit evidence-backed answers, and let GPT-6 Astra judge their work against a published rubric.

projects.title: GuitarRoll
projects.summary: Practice guitar with animated tabs, a synchronized piano visualization, selectable instrument tracks, and adjustable playback speed. Open a song and start playing in your browser. Built by a solo maker with GPT-6 Astra. Currently available in Spanish.
projects.summaryZh: GuitarRoll：在浏览器中用动态吉他谱、同步钢琴可视化、可选乐器轨和变速播放来练习吉他，目前仅支持西班牙语。
projects.summaryEn: Practice guitar with animated tabs, a synchronized piano visualization, selectable instrument tracks, and adjustable playback speed. Open a song and start playing in your browser. Built by a solo maker with GPT-6 Astra.

projects.title: Onhand
projects.summary: Onhand is a contextual AI for learning and research. It highlights the line, leaves a note in the margin, and explains it in the page you're already reading.
projects.summaryZh: 面向学习与研究的上下文AI，可在阅读页面高亮句子、在页边添加笔记并就地解释内容。
projects.summaryEn: Onhand is a contextual AI for learning and research. It highlights the line, leaves a note in the margin, and explains it in the page you're already reading.

projects.title: AINA
projects.summary: AINA is an AI career coach that helps you see what's holding your job search back, strengthen your profile, and practice for interviews — through conversations with a video avatar. Talk to AINA and walk away with a personalized action plan for whatever's next in your career.
projects.summaryZh: AI 职业教练，通过视频头像对话帮助求职者发现求职瓶颈、优化资料并模拟面试，制定职业行动计划。
projects.summaryEn: AINA is an AI career coach that helps you see what's holding your job search back, strengthen your profile, and practice for interviews — through conversations with a video avatar.

projects.title: CoAutoResearch
projects.summary: CoAutoResearch is an open-source research system where AI can run experiments, refine methods, and build research drafts — while humans stay in control. Review the direction, discuss findings, approve suggestions, pause when judgment is needed, and trace decisions and evidence throughout the research process.
projects.summaryZh: 开源AI研究系统，让AI运行实验、改进方法并撰写草稿，人类负责审核方向、讨论发现、批准建议、在需判断时暂停，并追踪决策与证据。
projects.summaryEn: CoAutoResearch is an open-source research system where AI can run experiments, refine methods, and build research drafts — while humans stay in control.

projects.title: Bookdam
projects.summary: Bookdam is a reading log for tracking what you're reading and saving the passages you want to remember. Snap a page, extract text with OCR, save quotes and notes, and revisit them anytime. Keep your reading history organized across iOS, Android, and the web.
projects.summaryZh: Bookdam 是一款阅读记录工具，可追踪阅读内容，通过 OCR 拍照摘录文字，保存书摘和笔记，支持 iOS、Android 和网页端。
projects.summaryEn: Bookdam is a reading log for tracking what you're reading and saving the passages you want to remember. Snap a page, extract text with OCR, save quotes and notes, and revisit them anytime.

projects.title: rockdata.app
projects.summary: Built to stay free. Always. rockdata.app is for people who love NFL research and want to understand why things happen. Using data from nflverse, we make player history, roles, opponents, and game context easier to explore. We believe every detail can influence future stats. All discoveries are public, so the community can question the evidence and learn together. We share research and discoveries, not picks.
projects.summaryZh: 面向 NFL 爱好者的免费数据研究平台，用 nflverse 数据探索球员历史、角色、对手和比赛背景，公开研究发现供社区讨论学习。
projects.summaryEn: Built to stay free. Always. rockdata.app is for people who love NFL research and want to understand why things happen. Using data from nflverse, we make player history, roles, opponents, and game context easier to explore.

projects.title: Zhenzhu

projects.title: Forseti
projects.summary: Forseti is an offline toolkit for pro se litigants using the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure. It provides fast rule search, motion templates, guides, deadlines, state rule PDFs, OCR scanning, case folders, notes, and bookmarks. No account, no data collection, and all files stay on‑device. A private, structured companion for navigating federal court.

projects.summaryEn: Forseti is an offline toolkit for pro se litigants using the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure. It provides fast rule search, motion templates, guides, deadlines, state rule PDFs, OCR scanning, case folders, notes, and bookmarks.

projects.title: OralInsulin MCP

It tracks clinical programs, market estimates, regulatory developments, manufacturers, partnerships and qualified relationship signals through MCP tools and a human-facing site. Built to help researchers, companies, investors and healthcare organizations evaluate evidence, compare claims and connect. Ask it anything: GPT-6 Astra answers by querying the same MCP

projects.summaryEn: OralInsulin MCP gives AI agents and human decision-makers a structured, source-backed view of the oral and oromucosal insulin landscape.

projects.summaryEn: Shishu is a living public history library. Read edited works, inspect sources and visible gaps beside the text, submit paragraph-level corrections, and follow version history. Public beta in English and Chinese.

projects.summaryEn: Product Graveyard is a digital cemetery for products that are no longer with us. Explore discontinued startups and apps, discover what they built, why they died, and the lessons their journeys left behind.

projects.title: Eco assess ai

It is built to make environmental assessment more organised, transparent, and efficient.

projects.summaryEn: EcoAssess AI brings environmental assessment into one workflow—combining document evidence, GIS screening, fieldwork, regulatory sources, impact and risk assessment, and report generation.

projects.title: motive.md
projects.summary: If OpenAI can solve a millennium prize problem with 30,000 agents, then why can't anyone contribute by crowdsourcing? Using the motive.md skill, agents follow a decentralized scientific method harness. Every contributor can pick up where the last one stopped. Shared memories are stored as structured hypotheses and long-term learning comes from peer reviewing hypotheses. The big picture: A conceptual UBI-in-tokens platform.
projects.summaryZh: 让智能体遵循去中心化科学方法框架，共享结构化假设并通过同行评审持续学习，实现众包科研协作。
projects.summaryEn: If OpenAI can solve a millennium prize problem with 30,000 agents, then why can't anyone contribute by crowdsourcing? Using the motive.md skill, agents follow a decentralized scientific method harness.

projects.title: Pokia

projects.summaryZh: Pokia 将 AI 概念转化为短小互动实验，让用户通过操纵检测器、训练样本和预测结果，直观探索 token、注意力与神经网络，并提供进阶实验室和免费学习路径。
projects.summaryEn: Pokia turns AI concepts into short, interactive experiments. Fool a detector, change its training examples, and see why its prediction changes. Explore tokens, attention and neural networks, then go deeper with Advanced labs.

projects.title: Dossier

Tell it what you want to know, and it generates a clear, cited research report — easy to understand, easy to save, ready to study whenever you need it. Built this because I wanted research to feel less like a chore and more like just... having the answer. Excited to share it here
projects.summaryZh: Dossier 根据你的问题生成清晰、带引用的研究报告，省去浏览标签页和记笔记的繁琐。
projects.summaryEn: Researching something new usually means hours of tab-hopping, half-read articles, and notes you'll never look at again. Dossier skips that part.

projects.title: 做了个读长文用的光带，顺带发现 bookmarklet 不受页面 CSP 管，但 loader 受
projects.author: keainiaikeke
projects.summary: 先说毛病：我读长文章，读到第三行就不知道自己在读哪一行了。 不是走神——注意力还在文章上,是"我刚才读到哪"这件事本身...,得回去重新扫一遍找那句。一篇长文读下来,大概三分之一的时间花在找行上。 所以写了一个： https://spotlightreading.com 贴个链接或者粘段文字进去就能读，也能直接开 txt / pdf / epub 。有条光带压在正在读的几行上，可以拖，可以点一句读一句，也可以按 F 让它跟着鼠标自动贴合整句或整段。 三个跟直觉相反的地方 1. 把其它行遮住是错的。 第一版我把光带以外的内容整个遮掉了，结果更难受——你会失去"自己在这一页什么位置"的空间感。现在的做法是光带以外的文字不遮，只让对比度沿梯度连续衰减。轮廓还在，但不抢注意力。 2. 虚化比变暗更糟。 早期版本是把周围文字 blur 掉，用起来明显更累。因为人看到模糊的东西会下意识地努力辨认，这个本能关不掉。改成单纯降对比之后，那些字读起来像"现在不轮到你"，而不是"这里坏了"。 3. 真正起作用的大头不是光带，是排版。 把文字重排成窄栏（中文一行 23 字左右、英文 65 字符左右）、行距拉到 2 倍上下，这一项的收益比光带还大。丢行主要发生在回扫那一瞬间——眼睛读完一行跳回下一行行首，行越长，落点误差越大。现在大部分网页一行四五十字，那是为了塞广告排的，不是为了给人读的。 几个实现上的坑 bookmarklet 不受页面 CSP 约束，但 loader 受。 书签工具我一开始按常规写法，在 bookmarklet 里 append 一个 。本地测得好好的，一到 Wikipedia 就死——Wikipedia 有 script-src CSP ，外部脚本直接被拦。而 Wikipedia 恰恰是最需要阅读辅助的地方。 解法是把整个压缩后的脚本内联进 javascript: URL 里，不走资源加载。因为 bookmarklet 是作为用户手势执行的，不算页面发起的资源请求，所以不受该页 CSP 管辖。6KB 塞在 href 里毫无压力。Wikipedia / MDN / BBC 实测都能跑。 CSS 自定义属性不 @property 注册，就没有过渡动画。 变暗的区域是一整个 gradient ，色标位置是 var(--t) 和 var(--b)。给它加 transition 完全没反应——自定义属性默认是无类型的，浏览器不知道怎么插值，只能在两个值之间硬跳，光带就是瞬移。用 @property { syntax: ' ' } 注册之后才开始滑动。 贴链接那条走 Worker 代抓。 浏览器有 CORS 进不去别人的站，所以 /api/read 由 Cloudflare Worker 代抓，用 HTMLRewriter 流式提取正文，扔掉导航、广告、侧栏、目录、语言列表。带 SSRF 防护（拒 localhost 、私有网段、非 http 协议）。 PDF 的断行要重新缝合。 pdf.js 拿到的文本是按排版切的，一句话经常被断成好几段。得按行高和右边界判断哪些是硬换行、哪些是排版导致的软换行，再缝回去，不然光带没法按句子贴合。 隐私 纯客户端。文件全部在浏览器里解析，不上传。没有账号，没有统计。只按文本指纹记住你上次读到哪——文本本身不存，只存位置。 做不到的 Canvas 渲染的阅读器（ Kindle 网页版这类把文字画成图的）只能整页染色，没法吸附句子。原生 App （微信读书、多看、Apple Books ）完全没有入口——这不是我偷懒，是不存在通道。 想听听： 你们读长文档丢行吗，还是只有我这样 手机上光带的拖动手感怎么样 还有哪些站的 CSP 会把书签工具挡住的，我想收集一下 （是我自己做的。）

projects.title: Show HN: A Mac native app that helps you reason through math/CS pdf textbooks
projects.author: alricsiu
projects.summary: https://marginstudy.lemonsqueezy.com/checkout/buy/b71656b9-b... url seems malformed The core concept is a tool to let users think through every word, sentence and line of dense technical textbooks in pdf form. I can't find a single app that allows you to reason about words and sentences while recording down your thoughts in a friction free way. All the note taking apps I've used treat paragraphs and pages as the main grouping element but anyone who's studied hard things knows that tough ideas are built up in groups of words at a time. Missing just one sentence before makes it impossible to understand the concepts further down. I wanted a way to let myself and others jot down ideas and partial understanding quickly and inline with the actual line that I'm struggling with. This lets me walk away from a problem and never lose any progress I made. It's almost like save checkpoints. The app also has another very nice scratchpad feature that lets you group notes from different areas of the textbook that talk about the same concept. It lets you relate topics from different parts of the textbook to form a cohesive picture of the material. I've also integrated Excalidraw into the scratch pad so you can take excalidraw diagram notes along with your note taking As an appreciation to Hacker News users for feedback, I made this pay what you want link as a token of appreciation. I've worked many sleepless nights to get this app as polished as it is and being able to afford to do this on my free time would be nice. The main product page is https://marginstudy.app/ . Would really appreciate feedback

projects.title: Show HN: I built a Mac app to make technical PDF textbooks easier to study
projects.author: alricsiu
projects.summary: I've always been a lifelong learner and have always tried to get through digital textbooks. Anyone who's used pdf textbooks know how much of a love/hate relationship it is. There are so many foundational textbooks published online for free now such as OSTEP, Modern Robotics, and Applied Linear Algebra just to name a few. - https://pages.cs.wisc.edu/~remzi/OSTEP/ - https://hades.mech.northwestern.edu/index.php/Modern_Robotic... - https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/vmls/ I've always preferred reading textbooks physically and writing inside them, but now with LLMs, it's nice to be able to just paste in passages to ChatGPT and ask for clarification. I've tried so many different types of digital note taking like Notability, Goodnotes, Margin Note, etc but none of them really made it easy for me to dive into dense material. I find myself getting distracted trying to take notes and forgetting what I just read. Out of my frustration, I decided to create my own tool and have been using it to get through my own personal studies. I built it around these core principles. - Technical textbooks are dense. I need to be able to quickly jot down a thought without distracting myself - I need to be able to pick up from where I left off quickly when I have quick bursts of inspiration to study - I need to be able to take scattered notes, and synthesize them into a cohesive subtopics so I can build on top of this knowledge as I progress in the textbook - Using the textbook needs to be fluid. It must be a good PDF reader first and foremost. I can safely say that what I've built is by far my favorite way to study any deep material. I'm able to take things line by line to truly understand how the author has built up their reasoning. This might be a biased view but firmly believe this tool could help anyone who have always tried learning new material. There are so many good free resources out there now, especially in AI, Math, Robotics. It's never been a better time to learn and I hope Margin helps anyone who's attempted to get through dense material as much as it has helped me.

projects.summary: 一个跑在个人电脑上的 AI 治理实验（自 2026-04 起运行和迭代，README 自述）。代理的会话承诺（hardboundaries）在动作出口被检查模型判定，判定违反的提议动作进入 L4 拒绝分支并记审计；治理文档与一份脱敏运行代码快照（约 260 文件含文档与许可证，占位符替换、不能直接跑，未公开范围 README 有列）均已公开，已知妥协逐条列在 README。配套运行代码仓： 亮点 机制公开可核查：classifier.py 负责对照会话承诺做检查并给出 L4 分类，willexecutor/main.py 执行拒绝并记录审计；承诺数据不可用或 hardboundaries 为空时检查跳过（保持默认分类），进入检查后出现调用异常/空输出/判决无法解析则拒绝（fail-closed）——两种路径都写在代码里。 带疤公开：宪法附件曾因程序执行遗漏晚落盘 18 天，补录文件明标「程序执行遗漏，非故意省略」并附复核签名（补录件=宪法/宪法入典生效-§13.3附件.md 的补录头）；README 列有事故名称、日期与档案去向。 操作者是不会写代码的学生，负责方向与争议裁决（README 自述）。

projects.author: ELONER
projects.summary: 现在 ai 时代，只要有想法就真的太容易实现了，不管是复刻，还是原创，一切都是那么的简单，就像我最近在搞的三个 ios app ，最初看了下 swift 语言语法和项目经典分层架构，然后约束了一下项目结构，后面全靠 AI 一点点的搞完了，争取这个月上架试试，有可能，也仅仅是满足了我自己的需求吧，不过也因此感受了不同模型的差异性，同一个模型不同版本之间差异真的不小，想想最差让 AI 实现我的想法，还很难一次性实现，让他生成 UI 设计图，还非常丑。但到后面，ai 生成的 UI 图一次比一次好看，好看到让我忍不住想立马体验这个 app ，可惜咯，AI 终究差了点，复刻 UI ，需要多次调整。就这样吧，大家要是对我的插件感兴趣，可以安装用用，给个评价，最初真就为了自己开发了个，后面发现也可以上架试试。 https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/mynote-ai-%E7%BD%91%E9%A1%B5%E5%88%86%E6%9E%90%E3%80%81markdown-%E4%B8%8E/iaejiichooljicpanlmfigjkdohakmij?authuser=0&hl=zh-CN 功能介绍： 提取网页正文或选区，使用自选 AI 模型进行分析、问答并生成 Markdown 笔记；支持本地历史、收藏、分组与笔记平台同步。 AI 核心提炼与忠实转写 基于选区或全文的连续问答 将问答整理为学习笔记 本地历史、搜索、收藏、分组与批量管理 Markdown 预览、复制和下载 语雀、Notion 、FlowUs 同步 多家模型及自定义 HTTPS 模型服务 我自己最常用的就是网页整理笔记功能和网页分析工具，比如网页整理成笔记功能，在看一篇很长的网页时，可以让他生成不同 浓度的笔记（浓缩、标准、扩展），然后快速对该网页内容有所了解，或者学习完内容后，可以快速让他生成核心笔记，等后续复习时候参考，然后再输出一篇作为自己的理解。后者网页分析，可以分析一下比如 V2EX 的 feed 列表和大家评论，了解有没有我感兴趣的内容，或者让他寻找热门。

projects.title: 【网站自荐】Textira：能查文献、跑实验、分析数据的 AI 科研工作台
projects.author: Baiang
projects.summary: 大家好，最近我们在做一个 AI 科研工作台 Textira，想推荐给周刊读者。 网站地址： Textira 想解决的问题其实很直接：现在 AI 已经能查文献、写代码、分析数据、生成图表，也能辅助写论文，但真正做一项研究时，这些事情依然散落在不同工具里。浏览器里查资料，本地保存 PDF 和数据，Jupyter 里跑代码，另一个窗口问 AI，实验完成后再把数据、图片、引用重新整理进论文。单独看，每一步都有很好用的工具，但从一个研究问题真正走到实验结果和论文，中间仍然需要大量人工衔接。 所以我们做 Textira 时，没有把它设计成一个单纯的 AI 聊天框或者论文生成器，而是以 Research 作为基本单位。一项研究里的文献、PDF、数据、代码、实验结果、图表和论文都可以放在同一个项目中，AI 也直接工作在这个环境里。你可以从一个研究问题开始，让它检索和阅读文献、寻找公开数据、编写并运行 Python、调用科研工具、分析实验结果、生成图表，再基于前面真实产生的材料继续完成后面的研究内容。 比如，我们曾经把 NASA TESS 的公开观测数据交给 Textira，尝试从恒星的光变曲线中寻找系外行星留下的凌日信号。这个任务不是让 AI 回答「如何寻找系外行星」，而是真的让它读取数据、编写分析代码、执行程序、寻找周期性变化并生成图表。如果中间的方法不合适，还可以根据实际运行结果继续修改代码和重跑实验。类似地，也可以给它一段蛋白质序列，让它调用相应工具完成结构预测和分析，或者直接上传自己的 CSV、Excel、代码和实验数据进行处理。 这也是我们比较在意的一点：AI 不应该只告诉研究者实验怎么做，而应该能够真正参与实验。 代码需要实际运行，数据需要实际处理，图表来自真实计算结果；任务过程中产生的数据、代码、图片和文件也都会留在 Research 中，后面的分析可以继续使用，而不是一次聊天结束以后重新从头解释。 论文则是这条链路自然的下一步。实验跑完以后，前面积累的文献、数据、代码、图表和实验结果仍然在同一个 Research 里，可以直接继续整理研究内容、处理引用和公式、调整结构和排版，并实时预览最终文档。Textira 支持完整的 LaTeX 项目，也可以导出常用文档格式，因此不需要实验结束以后，再把所有材料搬到另一个写作工具里重新开始。 我们希望这样还能解决 AI 辅助论文时一个很实际的问题：论文里的结果应该来自前面真正跑过的实验，而不是到了写作阶段再让模型“补”一组看起来合理的数据。 当实验和论文处在同一个研究上下文中，AI 可以继续使用真实的数据、图表和运行结果，研究者也更容易检查一个数字、一张图或者一个结论到底来自哪里。 所以 Textira 想做的并不是单独把某一个科研环节 AI 化，而是尽可能把一项研究连续起来： 研究问题 → 文献 → 数据 → 代码 → 实验 → 分析 → 图表 → 论文 目前 Textira 还在持续迭代。如果你手上正好有一个研究问题、一些实验数据，或者一篇正在进行中的论文，都可以直接拿来试试，也欢迎给我们反馈。 相关文章： 从序列到三维结构，Textira AI 如何预测蛋白质： 媒体报道 Textira 已获得 36Kr、钛媒体关注与报道。报道从 AI 科研与学术写作的实际需求出发，介绍了 Textira 如何将 AI 从论文写作环节进一步带入文献研究、实验、数据分析和投稿等科研流程。 36Kr 报道： Textira：

Inspired by the Ipsos Perils of Perception surveys, it's also an attempt to gamify testing our knowledge and biases. If this is interesting, you should also check out Perils of Perception: https://www.ipsos.com/en/perils/perils-perception-2024

projects.title: 开源 AI Study Platform，分享一下开发和部署踩坑
projects.author: spiderT

github.name: ttang1024/AI_Study_Platform
github.description: AI study platform for generating summaries, flashcards, quizzes, and mind maps from documents, videos, podcasts, and web articles.

projects.summary: 最近做了一个开源 AI 学习平台，希望把学习资料转化为完整的学习系统。 项目官网： https://toto-study.com GitHub： https://github.com/ttang1024/AI_Study_Platform 项目功能 支持上传 PDF 、添加 YouTube / Bilibili 视频、网页文章和播客，通过 AI 生成： Summary 和结构化学习笔记 Flashcards 、Quizzes 、Mind Maps 、Glossary AI Tutor ，针对学习内容进行问答 Spaced Repetition ，帮助复习记忆 使用时需要自行配置 AI API Key 。 这里分享两个实际生成的学习笔记： 1.总结文档内容： https://toto-study.com/share/AGC6GgQrjOJs 2.总结 YouTube 视频内容： https://toto-study.com/share/LQMBIdQunFJ5 两个开发和部署踩坑 1. YouTube 视频获取 本地开发时正常，部署到 AWS 后遇到了 bot detection 。参考社区建议，尝试使用 Residential IP 解决。体会到本地和云服务器的网络环境差异确实很大。 2. AWS 数据库成本 之前使用 AWS 的关系型数据库，个人项目每月成本有点高。这次将 PostgreSQL 迁移到外部 Supabase ，目前使用免费套餐，希望降低运行成本。 也想请教一下大家，个人项目一般是怎么控制 AWS 、数据库 这些长期运行成本的？

projects.summary: Reverse Video Search 是一个用于视频溯源和来源验证的在线工具。 做这个工具主要是因为现在一个视频被转载、裁剪、压缩、镜像、加字幕或者重新配音之后，单纯通过标题和关键词已经很难找到它最初的来源。 很多时候我们看到一段视频，真正想知道的其实不是“这个视频叫什么”，而是： 这个视频最早在哪里出现？ 是谁最先发布的？ 现在看到的版本是不是经过剪辑？ 有没有其他账号转载过？ 视频里的画面、声音或者水印能不能帮助找到原始来源？ 所以 Reverse Video Search 尝试从视频本身提取更多线索，而不是只搜索视频标题。 目前可以直接上传视频，也可以使用公开的视频 URL 或关键词进行搜索。 支持 MP4、MOV、AVI、WEBM 和 GIF，上传文件最大 50MB，视频最长 20 分钟。 核心的搜索方式是 Visual Fingerprinting。 系统会从视频中提取关键帧，然后寻找视觉上相似的内容。即使视频经过压缩、裁剪、调整大小或者镜像处理，也可以作为进一步寻找来源的线索。 除了画面之外，也可以从其他信号寻找匹配。 Audio Fingerprinting 可以比较视频中的音频，例如背景音乐、采访录音或者其他声音，即使相同的声音出现在不同的视频剪辑中，也可以作为搜索线索。 Transcript Match 可以使用 Whisper 对部分视频中的语音进行转录，然后利用说话内容寻找相关结果。 另外还有 OCR / Watermark Detection，可以读取视频关键帧中的文字、账号名称、Logo、水印和字幕。 这一点对于寻找转载视频的原始账号尤其有用。 比如一个视频被重新上传之后，原来的标题已经被修改，但是画面角落仍然保留着原作者的账号名称或者水印，那么这些信息就可能成为继续寻找来源的线索。 除了寻找相似视频之外，Reverse Video Search 也比较关注时间线。 找到可能的匹配之后，可以比较不同页面的发布日期、标题、字幕、水印和视频编辑情况，从而进一步判断哪个来源更早、更值得核实。 搜索结果还可以整理成 Evidence Report，把来源链接、日期、缩略图、匹配信息和备注放在一起。 这样如果是做事实核查、版权调查或者内容研究，就不用把所有找到的链接和截图分散保存。 目前这个工具主要适合几类场景。 如果你是内容创作者，可以用它寻找自己的视频是否被其他地方转载。 如果你是记者或事实核查人员，可以用它调查一段正在传播的视频，尝试找到更早的来源，并比较不同版本之间的差异。 如果你是品牌或代理机构，可以检查广告素材、品牌 Logo 或网红交付的视频是否出现在其他地方。 如果你是研究人员，也可以利用来源链接、日期、缩略图和编辑信息建立一个比较完整的视频来源记录。 当然，自动匹配并不能直接证明一个来源就是“原始来源”。 网站本身也把搜索结果定位为调查线索，而不是最终结论。 一些私人账号、已经删除的帖子、地区限制内容或者没有被索引的页面，系统可能无法访问。因此找到匹配之后，还是需要打开来源页面，比较日期、上下文和视频内容，再自己进行确认。 我觉得这也是视频反向搜索比较重要的一点： 不是让 AI 替你做最终判断，而是尽可能多地找到可以验证的证据。 如果你手里有一段不知道出处的视频，或者经常需要确认网络视频的来源，可以试试看： 目前可以先进行一次搜索，不需要账号；注册后还会获得额外 credits。 如果有人经常做视频溯源、事实核查或者版权调查，也欢迎分享一下你们平时都是怎么寻找视频原始来源的。

projects.title: Show HN: farseer.space – fly anywhere in the universe in your browser
projects.author: headsupernova
projects.summary: I've been hacking on a universe simulator, modeled on the path that the amazing SpaceEngine worked out over a decade ago, but without its Windows platform restriction. It takes real scientific data where we have it and augments it with procedural generation. So you can fly to e.g. the Whirlpool Galaxy, see a real image of it, but then fly into a 3d model that's created based on the image characteristics and visit individual stars etc within it. Same with nebula and other celestial objects. I used to work at a small planetarium during undergrad, and we didn't have the funds to buy the fancy planetarium software. I dreamed of using something like this during shows to share the scale of the cosmos with visitors. I've added a dome projection mode, but I haven't yet had the opportunity to test it out in a real planetarium yet. If anyone has access, let me know if it works! There's also a sorta hidden presentation share mode where you can share a link and others can follow along with your journey. I added this cause screen sharing so often compresses scenes like this to death! It worked ok for a quick share with some coworkers, but I'm sure there are some issues. Mobile controls are rough but maybe passable. Really hoping for feedback on how hard this thing is to use and where to improve! If you know of datasets I should be including or ways to improve rendering let me know! Anyway, happy flying! There is an incomprehensible amount of stuff happening out there!
